The famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg is the **RMS Titanic**.

To help you understand the complex concepts of blockchain technology described in the text, here are some analogies:

**1. The Digital Ledger as a Shared Notebook**
Imagine a group of friends who want to keep track of who owes whom money. Instead of one person holding the only notebook (which could be lost, stolen, or altered secretly), everyone in the group has their own identical copy of the notebook. This is the "decentralized" aspect.

**2. Immutability and Verification as a Group Consensus**
When someone wants to write a new entry in the notebook (like "Alice paid Bob $10"), they don't just write it in their own copy. They shout out the transaction to the group. Everyone checks their own notebook to make sure the transaction makes sense (e.g., Alice actually had $10). If the majority agrees it is valid, everyone writes it down in their own notebooks at the same time.

**3. Security through Redundancy**
If a hacker tries to break into one person's house and change their notebook to say "Alice paid Bob $1,000,000," it won't work. The other 999 people still have the correct record. Because the change wasn't agreed upon by the majority, the hacker's altered notebook is rejected as invalid. This makes the system "extremely secure and trustworthy" because no single point of failure exists, and altering history requires controlling the majority of the network simultaneously.
